label_source: named inside CLAUDE.md's Build Discipline section 6 at line 526. Read off, not assigned.
symptom: A component's load output was routed through a filter that dropped every line containing the word warning. One such line — a reference to a module that no longer existed — was printed on every single load for four months and was seen by nobody. It ended when the dead reference was reached at run time and brought down the test suite.
mechanism_as_described: The filter was installed deliberately, because the channel was noisy and the noise was not interesting. It removes lines by one fixed rule applied to every line, and it cannot tell a routine noisy line from a line reporting a genuinely broken reference — both contain the word. So a channel that was quiet because there was nothing to report and a channel that was quiet because everything it reported was being discarded produced the same output: nothing. Each part was individually sound. The load really did emit the line; the filter really did what it was written to do; the reader really did see a clean channel. The loss happens where the three meet, which is why no check at any one of them would have caught it.
detection_path: Reading the channel unfiltered, or replacing the blanket removal with a list of the specific lines that are permitted to be dropped, so that anything not on the list survives to the reader. Under that arrangement the dead-reference line has nowhere to go and appears on the first load.
consequence: A broken reference stayed live and invisible for four months and then failed at run time, in the suite, at the point where it was most expensive. The stated remedy is that a channel must carry an explicit list of what its silence is allowed to mean, rather than a blanket rule for what to throw away.
